name: Kokoro-82M
tagline: 82M params, Apache 2.0, runs on a potato

editorial.good_for: Excellent quality. Tiny model. Runs almost anywhere.

about: Kokoro is an 82-million-parameter text-to-speech model that consistently punches far above its weight, topping community TTS leaderboards against models many times its size. It ships with a set of polished preset voices and is fast enough to run in real time on modest hardware — which makes it even faster behind a hosted API.

name: Chatterbox
tagline: ElevenLabs-tier quality, MIT licensed, voice cloning from a clip

editorial.good_for: ElevenLabs-tier quality from a few seconds of reference audio.

about: Chatterbox is Resemble AI's open-source TTS model — a 0.5B-parameter system with zero-shot voice cloning from a few seconds of reference audio and a unique emotion-exaggeration control. In blind tests it's frequently preferred over leading commercial systems. Outputs include Resemble's PerTh watermark.

name: XTTS v2
tagline: Most-downloaded TTS on HF, 6-second voice cloning

editorial.pitch: The most-downloaded TTS on Hugging Face for a reason.

about: XTTS v2 is the flagship model of the Coqui TTS framework and one of the most widely used open voice-cloning models ever released. It clones a voice from a ~6-second sample and speaks 17 languages, with cross-language cloning — record in English, speak in Japanese. Coqui the company shut down, but the model remains a community staple.

name: Fish Speech
tagline: Open-source TTS that benchmarks above closed-source

editorial.pitch: Benchmarks above closed-source models on multilingual quality.

about: Fish Speech (and its successor OpenAudio) is a multilingual TTS family with strong zero-shot voice cloning across a dozen-plus languages, no phoneme dependency, and consistently top rankings on open TTS leaderboards. The hosted version skips its fairly heavy local setup.

name: Piper
tagline: Tiny, fast, runs offline on a Raspberry Pi
about: Piper is the workhorse of local text-to-speech — built by the Rhasspy voice-assistant project to run in real time on devices as small as a Raspberry Pi. It offers a huge catalog of community voices across dozens of languages. Through the API you get the same dependable output without managing voice files or ONNX runtimes.

name: Bark
tagline: Generates laughter, sighs, and music — the chaotic one

editorial.pitch: The chaotic one — generates laughter, sighs, even music. Use with intention.

about: Bark, from Suno, is a generative text-to-audio model rather than a plain TTS system. Beyond multilingual speech it produces laughter, sighs, crying, music, and background sounds from inline cues — trading precise control for creative range. Still unmatched for character and chaos.

name: F5-TTS
tagline: Flow-matching TTS, fast zero-shot voice cloning

editorial.pitch: Fast, flow-matched voice cloning. Zero-shot from a short reference.

about: F5-TTS uses flow matching with a diffusion transformer to produce fluent, faithful zero-shot voice clones from a single short reference. It became a community favorite for its simple architecture, fast inference, and surprisingly robust cloning quality.

name: Parler-TTS
tagline: Describe the voice in natural language ('soft female, fast, clear')
about: Parler-TTS, from Hugging Face's audio team, takes a different approach: instead of cloning a reference, you describe the speaker in text — "a calm female voice with a slight British accent, speaking slowly" — and it synthesizes that voice. Fully open training code and data recipes.

name: Dia
tagline: Ultra-realistic two-speaker dialogue, sounds like a podcast

editorial.pitch: Sounds like a podcast — two-speaker dialogue out of the box.

about: Dia generates full conversations directly from screenplay-style text — tag lines with [S1] and [S2] and it renders a natural two-voice dialogue in a single pass, complete with laughs, coughs, and throat-clears. A 1.6B model that went viral for podcast-style output rivaling paid tools.

name: CosyVoice 2
tagline: Alibaba's real-time TTS, 150ms streaming latency
about: CosyVoice 2 from Alibaba's FunAudioLLM team is engineered for real-time use: streaming synthesis at roughly 150ms first-packet latency with quality nearly identical to offline mode. It supports zero-shot cloning, cross-lingual synthesis, dialect control, and natural-language instructions over emotion and style.

name: IndexTTS 2
tagline: Bilibili's TTS with multi-speaker and precise emotion control
about: IndexTTS 2, from Bilibili, targets professional dubbing: it's the rare autoregressive TTS with explicit duration control (hit an exact clip length) and disentangled emotion control — take the voice from one reference and the emotion from another, or steer it with text.

name: VibeVoice
tagline: Microsoft's long-form TTS — 90 minutes, 4 speakers
about: VibeVoice is Microsoft's long-form TTS: it can synthesize up to ~90 minutes of continuous audio with up to four distinct speakers in a single generation — built for podcast-style content. Ultra-low-frame-rate tokenizers keep generation efficient despite the scale.

name: Qwen3-TTS
tagline: Alibaba's flagship, 97ms latency, 10 languages
about: Qwen3-TTS is the text-to-speech line from Alibaba's Qwen team, known for strong multilingual coverage — including Chinese dialects like Cantonese, Wu, and Sichuanese — with expressive preset voices and fast synthesis backed by the Qwen model family.

name: Orpheus TTS
tagline: Llama-3 based, empathetic, low-latency for interactive apps

editorial.good_for: Llama-3 based. Empathetic. Built for interactive apps.

about: Orpheus is a Llama-3B-based speech model from Canopy Labs. It generates remarkably human intonation and supports inline emotive tags like laughter and sighs, plus zero-shot voice cloning and low-latency streaming. One of the most natural conversational voices in open source.

name: KittenTTS
tagline: 15M params, under 25MB, runs anywhere — even your phone
about: KittenTTS is an ultra-lightweight English TTS model — around 15 million parameters, small enough to run without a GPU entirely. It trades some expressiveness for extreme efficiency, with a handful of clean preset voices. Via the API it's effectively instant.

name: OpenVoice v2
tagline: Tone-color cloning + cross-lingual transfer
about: OpenVoice v2 clones the tone color of a reference speaker and then lets you control style — emotion, accent, rhythm, pauses, intonation — independently. It supports cross-lingual cloning into languages the reference speaker never spoke, and v2 moved to a permissive MIT license.

name: StyleTTS 2
tagline: Diffusion-based, human-level naturalness on LibriTTS
about: StyleTTS 2 made waves by reaching human-level naturalness on standard English benchmarks using style diffusion and adversarial training with large speech-language models. It supports zero-shot speaker adaptation from a short reference clip and remains a favorite for natural prosody.

name: MeloTTS
tagline: Multilingual, real-time on CPU
about: MeloTTS from MyShell.ai is one of the most-downloaded open TTS models on Hugging Face. It covers English (with multiple accents), Spanish, French, Chinese, Japanese and Korean, and was designed for real-time inference even on CPU. A clean, dependable choice for multilingual products.

name: Spark-TTS
tagline: Built on Qwen2.5, zero-shot voice cloning + style control
about: Spark-TTS builds speech generation directly on a 0.5B Qwen backbone with a single-stream codec, making it unusually simple and efficient. It does zero-shot cloning plus controllable voice creation — set gender, pitch, and speaking style to synthesize a new voice from scratch.

name: MegaTTS 3
tagline: ByteDance's TTS with sparse alignment — robust prosody
about: MegaTTS 3 is ByteDance's open release: a compact 0.45B diffusion-transformer TTS with high-quality zero-shot cloning, bilingual Chinese/English support with code-switching, and unusual extras like adjustable accent intensity for pronunciation control.

name: WhisperSpeech
tagline: Whisper, but inverted — TTS by 'unwrapping' OpenAI's ASR
about: WhisperSpeech, from Collabora, flips OpenAI's Whisper architecture around to generate speech instead of transcribing it. It's trained entirely on properly licensed open data — a deliberately transparent, commercially safe stack — with voice cloning from reference audio.

name: Higgs Audio v2
tagline: Built on Llama 3.2 3B, 10M+ hours of training audio
about: Higgs Audio v2 builds audio generation on top of a Llama-3-class language model trained on 10M+ hours of audio. It wins the majority of emotion benchmarks against leading commercial models and does things few others can: multi-speaker dialogue, melodic humming, and voice cloning with deep prosody understanding.

name: GPT-SoVITS
tagline: The community's favorite few-shot voice-cloning toolkit
about: GPT-SoVITS has one of the largest communities in open voice AI. It does zero-shot cloning from a few seconds of audio, but its signature trick is few-shot training: with just one minute of a voice it produces a dramatically more faithful clone. That workflow made it the de facto standard for hobbyist voice cloning, especially across the Chinese and Japanese communities.

name: Sesame CSM-1B
tagline: The conversational speech model behind the viral Maya demo
about: CSM-1B is the open model from Sesame, whose 'Maya' assistant demo went viral for sounding uncannily present — breath, hesitation, tone shifts and all. It generates speech conditioned on conversation context, so replies sound like part of a dialogue rather than isolated lines. The open release is the base generation model behind that demo.

name: Zonos
tagline: 44kHz studio-quality output with emotion control
about: Zonos from Zyphra generates native 44kHz audio — noticeably crisper than the 22-24kHz most open models produce — with zero-shot cloning from a short reference and explicit control over emotions like happiness, sadness, and anger. It ships in both pure-transformer and SSM-hybrid variants.

name: NeuTTS Air
tagline: On-device-class TTS with instant cloning from ~3 seconds
about: NeuTTS Air from Neuphonic is built to run in real time on a CPU — a ~0.7B-parameter model on a Qwen backbone that still manages instant voice cloning from around three seconds of reference audio. It's designed for on-device privacy, which also makes it one of the cheapest modern TTS models to serve.
